title: Transducing quantum-spin-ice correlations into Weyl Fermi-arc transport at a synthetic Kondo lattice interface
authors: Tsung-Chi Wu, Michael Terilli, Christian Zaprianov, Eun Sang Choi, David Graf, Qinghua Zhang, Lin Gu, Mikhail Kareev
abstract: Quantum spin ice hosts collective excitations and quantum fluctuations that are largely electrically silent because the materials supporting them are insulating. Coupling this magnetic environment to surface-localized Weyl states offers a route to encode its correlations directly into Fermi-arc transport. Experimental access to this regime, however, has remained largely unexplored. Here, we realize a synthetic Kondo lattice interface between the Weyl semimetal $\mathrm{Eu_2Ir_2O_7}$ and the quantum-spin-ice candidate $\mathrm{Tb_2Ti_2O_7}$, and demonstrate that quantum-spin-ice correlations are imprinted on Weyl Fermi-arc transport. At ultra-low temperature, electronic transport evolves from a sixfold anisotropic response at low field into a twelvefold response over an intermediate field window, before entering a reentrant sixfold anisotropy at high field. No analogous twelvefold response occurs at the classical-spin-ice interface. The quantum--classical contrast shows that the same itinerant electronic channel acquires qualitatively different symmetry information when interacting with the quantum-fluctuating Tb moments, consistent with an interfacial coupling between the Weyl surface states and the transverse, multipolar degrees of freedom, in addition to the longitudinal, dipolar contribution. Our work establishes synthetic Kondo lattice interfaces as a route for transducing frustrated quantum magnetism with multipole correlations into distinct Weyl Fermi-arc transport responses.
summary: The authors demonstrate a novel method to probe quantum-spin-ice correlations by coupling them to Weyl semimetal surface states via a synthetic Kondo lattice interface. By measuring the angular magnetoresistance, they observe a unique twelvefold symmetry reconstruction only when coupled to a quantum spin-ice candidate ($	ext{Tb}_2	ext{Ti}_2	ext{O}_7$). This confirms that the electronic transport acts as a sensitive transducer for the underlying multipolar quantum magnetic order.
main_problem: The study aims to demonstrate a method to encode and detect quantum-spin-ice correlations, particularly those involving multipolar degrees of freedom, into measurable electronic transport properties.
main_result: The quantum-spin-ice interface ($	ext{Tb}_2	ext{Ti}_2	ext{O}_7$) exhibits a unique $	ext{6-fold} 	o 	ext{12-fold} 	o 	ext{6-fold}$ reentrant anisotropy in the angular magnetoresistance, a signature absent in the classical spin-ice reference ($	ext{Dy}_2	ext{Ti}_2	ext{O}_7$).
method: The research uses in-plane and out-of-plane angular magnetoresistance measurements on a synthetic Kondo lattice interface at ultra-low temperatures.
model_or_system: The platform is a synthetic Kondo lattice interface formed between a Weyl semimetal ($	ext{Eu}_2	ext{Ir}_2	ext{O}_7$) and a quantum-spin-ice candidate ($	ext{Tb}_2	ext{Ti}_2	ext{O}_7$), allowing the coupling of itinerant Weyl surface states to frustrated local moments.
key_observables: Angular magnetoresistance ($	ext{MR}$), specifically the symmetry reconstruction observed as a transition from sixfold to twelvefold anisotropy ($	ext{MR}_{12}/	ext{MR}_6$).
important_parameters: Ultra-low temperatures ($	ext{20 mK}$), varying magnetic field strength, and the comparison between quantum ($	ext{Tb}$) and classical ($	ext{Dy}$) spin-ice couplings.
main_assumptions: The electronic transport is sensitive to the specific magnetic degrees of freedom (dipolar vs. multipolar) present in the adjacent spin-ice material.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the structural interface, the field evolution of angular magnetoresistance showing the $	ext{6-fold} 	o 	ext{12-fold} 	o 	ext{6-fold}$ sequence for the quantum case, and direct comparisons with the classical case.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical system, details the measurement techniques (ADMR), presents the key comparative results showing the distinct symmetry signatures ($	ext{12-fold}$ vs. $	ext{2-fold}$), and concludes by establishing the synthetic Kondo lattice as a transduction route.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly tunable, solid-state platform to probe exotic quantum magnetic correlations (multipolar moments) by mapping them onto measurable electronic transport symmetries, which is relevant for understanding strongly correlated interfacial physics.
